operating_notes.text: Aerospace segment revenue grew 22% YoY to ₹172.8 Cr in Q4FY25.
Hydraulics segment reported a loss of ₹5.16 Cr in Q4FY25 versus a profit of ₹3.92 Cr in Q4FY24.
Metallurgy segment revenue declined 11% YoY to ₹94.43 Cr in Q4FY25.

Dynauton Systems, Dynamatic's unmanned-systems division set up in 2023, signed an MoU with Aerodata AG on 22 April 2026 to evaluate Aerodata's AeroForce X MALE UAS (endurance up to 40 hours) for the Indian market.
Aerospace segment FY26 revenue ₹775.61 Cr vs ₹607.85 Cr prior year, segment profit ₹132.39 Cr.
DLUK hydraulics division transferring specific production operations to India while retaining select strategic product lines in the UK.
A non-cash tax charge of INR 562 lakhs was recognised in DLUK on intra-group IP transfer, impacting the Group's effective tax rate.
Aerospace segment revenue reached ₹775.61 Cr in FY26, up 27.6% YoY.
India Ratings affirmed Dynamatic Technologies' bank loan facilities at IND A with a Stable outlook.
UAV vertical being transferred to Dynauton Limited includes R&D, WIP, inventories, and intellectual property.
Dynauton Limited had nil turnover in FY26.

timeline.summary: Q4FY25 results (consolidated): revenue ₹380.67 Cr, net profit ₹16.09 Cr.
2026-04-22: Dynauton Systems, a division of Dynamatic, signed an MoU with Germany's Aerodata AG to jointly develop an unmanned airborne surveillance and reconnaissance solution for India.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹433.16 Cr (+13.8% YoY), net profit ₹12.56 Cr (-21.9% YoY).
Dynamatic Technologies reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹433.16 Cr (+13.8% YoY) and FY26 revenue of ₹1,621.34 Cr.
India Ratings affirmed Dynamatic Technologies' bank loan facilities at IND A with a Stable outlook.
Dynamatic Technologies approved the slump sale of its UAV vertical to subsidiary Dynauton Limited for ₹29.18 Cr and a ₹45 Cr preferential issue in the subsidiary.
